leads.name: The Weeping Silver Lime of Scheteldoekshaven
verified_sources: Gemeente Alkmaar, 'Lijst monumentale en waardevolle bomen in Alkmaar', March 2017 (openpdc.alkmaar.nl PDF), entry: Hangende zilverlinde, Tilia tomentosa Pendula, Bolwerk thv Scheteldoekshaven 5, 1930-1940
leads.access: Free. Public park on the old city rampart (Bolwerk).
leads.transport: Central Alkmaar, short walk from Alkmaar Centraal station
leads.story:
In a strong wind this tree changes colour. The underside of a silver lime's leaf is covered in fine white felt, which is what tomentosa means, so one gust turns a green crown pale grey and the next turns it back.

This one is the weeping form, Tilia tomentosa 'Pendula', and both the national register and the city's own 2017 list of monumental trees name the cultivar outright. The branches hang rather than reach, so the colour change runs from the top of the crown all the way down, like a curtain being shaken out.

It stands on the Bolwerk, the belt of old earthworks Alkmaar stopped defending and started walking on. The two sources agree on the decade as well as the species: it went into the ground somewhere between 1930 and 1940, which makes it a young tree with an unusual shape at the point the occupation arrived, and it has held the same spot on the rampart ever since.

Beyond that, nothing. The register's history field for this lime reads onbekend, unknown. Nobody has written down who planted it or why a weeping silver lime was the choice for this corner of the park. If you know, tell us and it goes on the page.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the branches hanging straight down in a curtain and by leaves that flash white-grey underneath in the wind. It stands in the rampart park opposite Scheteldoekshaven 5.
leads.removed_reason: Dead or felled per the register itself: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen nr 1690998 carries status 5, Dood/geveld (checked 2026-10-10 against the Bomenstichting ArcGIS layer). Inspector remark: "Geënt op 150 cm." Removed under the rule that a dead tree is never a collectible entry.

leads.name: The Horse Chestnut behind Koekenbier

location.address: About 25 metres into the woods behind restaurant Koekenbier, Kennemerstraatweg

leads.transport: Central Alkmaar, roughly 15-20 minute walk or short bus ride from Alkmaar Centraal station
leads.story:
The national register lists this horse chestnut with almost nothing beside it: no planting date, no note on its history, the field left onbekend, unknown. What is fixed is where it stands, about twenty-five metres into the trees behind restaurant Koekenbier, off the Kennemerstraatweg, on the edge of the Alkmaarderhout.

The register bands its age at roughly a century and a quarter without saying how that figure was reached, which would put its planting close to the years around 1900 when the landscape architect L.A. Springer rebuilt the park into its present form. That is inference rather than record, and the register does not claim otherwise.

A horse chestnut this size has gone through the same year over and over regardless of what got written down: white candle-shaped flower spikes standing through the crown in May, spiked green conkers splitting on the ground by October. None of that is recorded for this particular tree, only for the species in general.

It stands roughly a hundred metres from the park's copper beech and about 300 metres from its oldest recorded plane, part of the same walk through the Westerhoutpark. If you know more about it, tell us.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the white candle-shaped flowers in May and the spiky green conkers underfoot by October. It stands about twenty-five metres into the woods behind restaurant Koekenbier, off the Kennemerstraatweg.
leads.removed_reason: Dead or felled per the register itself: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen nr 1689039 carries status 5, Dood/geveld (checked 2026-10-10 against the Bomenstichting ArcGIS layer). Inspector remark: "In het park op kruispuntje van wandelpaden." Removed under the rule that a dead tree is never a collectible entry.

blocked.name: Bruine beuk (Copper Beech), near the music garden/flower clock, Alkmaarderhout
blocked.location_hint: LRMB register nr 1684912, 52.625128,4.734696, planted_band 1800-1850, about 25-50m from already-published alk_003 (The Plane of the Alkmaarderhout)
blocked.reason: DEAD. The register's own site_history is explicit: 'Helaas is de beuk gesneuveld in de Polystorm van de zomer 2023. Tot bijna vier meter hoogte staat de stam nog overeind' (the beech fell in Storm Poly, summer 2023; the trunk still stands to almost four metres). Independently confirmed that Storm Poly struck Alkmaar on 5 July 2023, felling 500+ trees and severely damaging roughly 200 more across the municipality (Rodi.nl news report; gemeente Alkmaar's own storm-damage recovery page, 'Herstel schade storm Poly'). A stump, however tall, is not a collectible entry per 'we doen niet aan dode bomen'. Do not confuse with the nearby still-standing alk_013 (Copper Beech of the Hertenkamp, register nr 1688896), which is a different, separate specimen about 800m away with no storm-damage note in its own register history.

blocked.name: Hollandse iep, against the historic ice cellar (ijskeldertje/kruithuisje), Geest/Bolwerk
blocked.reason: DEAD, felled. Confirmed by two independent sources: NH Nieuws ('Oude iep gekapt om Alkmaars rijksmonument te redden') and Alkmaar Centraal / Streekstad Centraal ('Iep op Bolwerk moet weg vanwege schade aan monument en ziekte', with a follow-up 'Monumentale iep op Alkmaars Bolwerk nu echt weg' video). The elm's roots were damaging the walls and roof of the adjacent listed ice cellar (a rijksmonument) and the tree itself had Dutch elm disease despite annual inoculation; permitting began in early 2018 and the tree was felled in January 2019. The LRMB register entry itself carries no vitality flag and would otherwise read as a live, publishable tree, which is exactly the register-pitfall this project's rules warn about. Confirmed distinct from all trees delivered this pass (different address, 'tegen buskruid/ijskeldertje', not matched to any of alk_008 through alk_014).
